clue.text: A Fonteyn ruined by Alan, a US ballet impresario? Not 'e!

indicators.note: the words that follow are wrecked and rebuilt into a new order
says the next item is to be left out of the jumbled letters

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged, less one E
the Cockney 'e is a dropped-aitch he, standing for the bare letter E

explanation.surface: A tetchy note that an American dance producer called Alan wrecked Margot Fonteyn's performance, with a jab that he is no gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIMA BALLERINA ASSOLUTA is the rare top title for a ballerina, held by Dame Margot Fonteyn. Of the two Es in the fodder, one is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Margot Fonteyn was named to this supreme ballet rank, so the title describes her as one example of its holders.

clue.text: Condition arising from 8's 27 with 12: 'ope Rex had clamp fitted!

definitions.note: a cradle-snatcher's sex with a stepchild

indicators.note: the letters are fitted together in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dropped-aitch hope that King Oedipus Rex had his swollen feet clamped, playing on the more famous Oedipus complex.
explanation.walkthrough: Phaedra, wife of Theseus, fell for her stepson Hippolytus; the psychological term for a step-parent's desire for a stepchild is named after her.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a step-parent's sexual attraction to a stepchild, after the Greek queen who desired her husband's son.

clue.text: Maigret's outfit docked with crown dependencies over jaundice

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned over means read from the bottom upwards
cut off at the tail, like a docked tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the Sûreté, the French detective force Simenon's Maigret belongs to
the Channel Islands, CI, are British Crown dependencies

explanation.surface: The French police force, trimmed and joined with some offshore islands, looks rather yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: ICTERUS is the medical name for jaundice.
explanation.definitionFit: Icterus is the clinical term for the yellowing of skin and eyes that the everyday word jaundice describes.

clue.text: To the French, RUC liar confounded hearing

parts.note: au is French for 'to the'

indicators.note: mixed up and confused, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lying officer of the Royal Ulster Constabulary is exposed to the French at a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police force until 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: Auricular means relating to the ear or to hearing, as in auricular confession, spoken into the ear.

clue.text: A quiet location for Postman Pat!

definitions.note: here an adjective, as in a pat answer

parts.note: taken as written
P, piano, the musical direction for soft
the post office is the PO, and its location is the PO site

explanation.surface: A peaceful village for the children's TV character Postman Pat.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's TV postman, but 'Pat' is the adjective meaning apt, as in 'a pat reply'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean exactly fitting or apt, as when a remark is well suited to the moment.

clue.text: Gold digging queen digs user

indicators.note: dug up and turned over, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A gold-digging queen who dislikes users, a moralising snapshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' reads as a verb; it is the British noun for rented rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodger lives in someone's rented rooms, British 'digs', so is a person making use of them.

clue.text: Cecil Ericson turned out a bit of a saint

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned means the letters read upwards
the answer is found lying out within the run of the two names

parts.note: the name whose run of letters holds the answer

explanation.surface: A man named Cecil Ericson proved to be something of a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of a saint' sounds like 'fairly saintly' but means a piece of a saint's body kept as an object of veneration.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a bone or other bodily fragment of a holy person preserved for veneration.

clue.text: Casually dressed gentile with time off for good behaviour

indicators.note: the way the letters behave is changed, so they are reordered
the time letter comes off and the good letter goes in its place

parts.note: taken as written: the word whose letters are adjusted
T, standard abbreviation for time
G, standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A non-Jew in casual clothes is granted remission for good behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time off for good behaviour' is prison remission, but here it splits into separate instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Négligé, from French, describes someone in informal or partial dress, as in a loose house gown.

clue.text: Stand clear, cher offspring! This rake's after you!

indicators.note: the letters spring off in different directions and come back in another order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning to a French darling's children to step aside because a lecherous man is coming for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle-snatcher is someone who courts a much younger partner, a lecher who chases youth.

clue.text: Once and future king, banning university work, starts on doodle bug

indicators.note: barring the university letter from the king's name, so it is taken out

parts.note: T. H. White's novel title for King Arthur
U is the standard abbreviation for university
OP, short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of the two following words is used

parts.note: the words whose first letters are taken

explanation.surface: An oddly listed piece of Arthurian trivia beside some idle scribbling of an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doodle bug' reads as one thing (a WW2 flying bomb, or an ant-lion larva), but only 'bug' defines; 'doodle' supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are arthropods, and bug is a loose everyday word for any small creepy-crawly of that phylum.

clue.text: Cubist canonised at Doncaster?

definitions.meaning: Fernand Léger, the French Cubist painter
the classic horse race run at Doncaster, so the name gets a saint's title there

explanation.walkthrough: Doncaster is a racing town in Yorkshire; its famous race, the St Leger, makes the painter's surname look sainted.
explanation.definitionFit: Léger was a leading Cubist painter, and the same surname appears in a racing title with a Saint prefix.

clue.text: Holliday corralling smallest state order

indicators.note: penning in, as cattle in a corral, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Doc Holliday, the Wild West gunfighter
Rhode Island, the smallest US state, abbreviated RI

explanation.surface: Doc Holliday rounding up an instruction from a tiny state, a Wild West scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' sounds like a command, but it is the architectural sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of architecture, the column style along with Ionic and Corinthian.

clue.text: A chip off the defunct block?

definitions.text: A chip off the defunct block?

parts.note: the idiom for a child who resembles a parent
the old block replaced by a dead one: the parent is gone and a new one has stepped in

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase twists 'a chip off the old block': the child of a parent who has died and whose place a new partner has taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A child of one's spouse by an earlier marriage, often one whose own parent has died, is called by this name.

clue.text: See 1
Yank gently affected nameless form of Buddhism

indicators.note: without a name, so the name abbreviation N is taken out of the Buddhist school

parts.note: twee means affectedly dainty or quaint
Zen, the meditative Japanese school

explanation.surface: An American with a precious manner takes up an anonymous brand of Buddhism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American person; here it is the verb to pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To pluck something out with tweezers is a small, careful pull, a delicate tug.

clue.text: Parisian leaves producer, dead now, to raise support for Ms Herzigova

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the letters reads them from the bottom up

parts.note: arbre is French for tree, the thing that produces leaves
D, abbreviation used in records and family trees
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French producer has died and a model's supporters rally to her.
explanation.walkthrough: Eva Herzigova was the Czech model in the famous 'Hello Boys' Wonderbra poster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wonderbra is a push-up brassiere brand, the garment Herzigova famously advertised.

clue.text: Foothold for climber caught in a transmitter

indicators.note: the caught letter is placed inside the transmitter word

parts.note: a sender is a transmitter
C, the cricket scorebook abbreviation

explanation.surface: A climber's footing is captured on a radio transmitter.
explanation.walkthrough: An ascender is a gripping device that climbers clamp to a rope and stand or pull on.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers fix a foot loop to this rope-clamp to step upward, so it gives them a hold for the foot.

clue.text: Inspired after scratching the match?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fired with enthusiasm, at one's brilliant best
second meaning: a match struck on its box is literally burning

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratching the match' suggests withdrawing from a game; it means striking a matchstick.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer playing brilliantly is said to be burning hot in this idiom, and a struck match is literally alight.

clue.text: Priest in dog collar creating opera

indicators.note: the priest goes inside the dog, which acts as a collar round him

parts.note: Fido, a stock name for a dog, forming the collar round the priest
Eli, the biblical priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A clergyman in his dog collar puts on an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog collar' looks like a clerical collar on the priest; the dog's name wraps round him instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidelio is Beethoven's only opera.

clue.text: League's successors investing a chip off the old block's capital

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the United Nations initials are put into the other piece

parts.note: a scion is a descendant, a child of the family
the UN succeeded the League of Nations

explanation.surface: The League of Nations' heirs put money into the son of an old family.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunción is the capital city of Paraguay.

clue.text: The rain falls in Bury!

indicators.note: the letters tumble down and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: It is pouring in Bury, the rainy Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town near Manchester; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inearth is an old poetic verb for putting into the ground, that is, interring.

clue.text: Benign aroma surrounding Spenser's fool

indicators.note: the outer clue words surround the answer, which lies within them

parts.note: the words that hold the answer

explanation.surface: A pleasant smell hangs about a foolish character in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignaro is the foolish old porter in Spenser's The Faerie Queene, whose name means ignorant.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Faerie Queene the dim-witted keeper of Orgoglio's castle bears this name, Italian for ignoramus.

clue.text: Daughter, after training, eager to hear teacher

indicators.note: places the daughter's letter behind the training

parts.note: PE, physical education, school exercise
D, the standard abbreviation

indicators.note: the word for eager is taken as it is spoken, and the spelling changes

parts.note: agog means eagerly expectant

explanation.surface: A daughter, fresh from training, longs to listen to her teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The word's ending is pronounced like agog, so the sound is kept and the spelling becomes -AGOGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a schoolmaster, now often used of a strict or pedantic instructor.

clue.text: Confines spectators

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to gate is to keep a pupil inside school grounds as a punishment
second meaning: the gate is the number of people attending a sports match

explanation.walkthrough: Gating a pupil is British school slang for confining them, and a football gate is the crowd that paid to enter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for keeping someone in as a punishment and a noun for the paying attendance at a match.

clue.text: Permission to travel with old fare

parts.note: EX means former
to fare is to eat, food being fare

explanation.surface: Leave to journey comes with some old-fashioned food.
explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is the British school or college pass that lets a pupil leave for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin 'let him go out' names a formal leave of absence from a school or college.

clue.text: City nearly dead from success

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
late means deceased

explanation.surface: A town nearly wiped out by its own prosperity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' is the City of London, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliant success or acclaim, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Festival site burgled. Ah, calamity!

indicators.note: a disaster that scrambles everything, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone discovers the festival grounds have been robbed and cries out in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: ALDEBURGH is a Suffolk seaside town whose music festival was founded by Benjamin Britten.
explanation.definitionFit: This English coastal town hosts a famous annual music festival, so it is a well-known festival venue.

clue.text: Congress house worthy? Far from it!

indicators.note: the exclamation says the letters are far from their proper arrangement, so they are reordered

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A scornful aside that a chamber like Congress hardly deserves respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' seems to be the US legislature; it means sexual intercourse. 'A bit of how's your father' is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Congress is a formal word for sexual intercourse, and this British slang phrase is a coy euphemism for the same act.
